content.thinking:
I need to write this whole module carefully in one pass without verification, designing a safe but rich structure using plain geometry objects and lathe/extrude/sweep builders. I'm thinking through joints too—since parts need exactly one root joint, I'll set up a root joint at the origin so props placed with `at` can attach to the nearest joint.

I'll keep the skeleton minimal: just a root joint plus maybe two hinge joints for hanging lanterns, avoiding unnecessary complexity. For style I'm aiming for a Genshin-inspired toon cel look with vermilion torii gates, gold filigree, and glow accents, using cel-shaded paint on geometry parts since lighting depends only on normals.

Now I'm sketching helper functions for boxes and cylinders, then laying out the torii structure in meters—placing the two vermilion pillars, designing the upswept kasagi beam via an extruded outline, and positioning the lower nuki beam.

I'm extending the layout past the torii: a central plaque, black-capped pillar bases, a black kasagi underside, and shide paper zigzags hanging from the shimenawa rope. Behind the torii I'm adding a small hokora shrine with stone steps, a gabled roof built from two angled boxes, gold-trimmed doors, and a small bell. Then I'm placing a pair of stone tōrō lanterns flanking the path, each with a lathed base and roof, a glowing firebox window, and a hoju sphere finial on top.

Now I'm laying out stone path slabs leading from the torii, a mottled gravel ground disc, and hanging chochin paper lanterns strung between the pillars. I'm also adding offerings and details — a sake barrel, fruit and rice bowls, a pair of kitsune statues built from capsules and cones, dango, candles, flowers, incense, and a small sakura tree with a swept trunk and flat icosphere canopy blossoms.

I'm sketching floating teal glow orbs near the shrine with a spiral wind-swirl motif, planning simple SVG textures for the ema plaque, torii text, and lantern decals, and settling on a limited flat/cel color palette with helper functions for building parts.

Defining palette colors...

Now I'm setting up the joint hierarchy, starting with a root joint and hinge joints for swinging elements like the lantern.

I'm also designing the shrine's bell with a hinge joint and rope attachment, plus using lathe shapes for ring-like forms built from rotated outlines. For the torii gate, I'm sweeping pillar shapes with tapered radii, circular cross-sections, and vermilion paint, topped with black cylindrical bases.

Now I'm working out the kasagi (top lintel) shape as an extruded outline, defining a sequence of points that curve upward from the bottom-left edge, along the base, up through the right end, and back across the top with a gentle arc.

I'm giving the kasagi a vermilion top with a black underlay beam, sizing the pillar heights so their tops stay hidden beneath it, then adding the nuki crossbeam as a vermilion box with ends protruding past the pillars.

Now I'm placing the gakuzuka plaque between the nuki and the top beam, giving it a black body with a gold frame and a textured front face, plus gold rings at the nuki-pillar junctions. I'm positioning the torii and shrine along the z-axis with a path connecting them, and starting the hokora's stone base dimensions on the ground disc.

Next I'm building the shrine body with wood-grain pillars, cream doors with gold lattice texture, and a gabled roof made of two sloped slabs plus a ridge cylinder with gold end caps -- working out the rotation angles so the slopes tilt correctly along the x-axis while the ridge runs along z.

I'm adding the front gable triangle as a thin extruded shape positioned at the roof peak, checking that its edges align with the sloped roof underside so it doesn't poke through.

Now I'm planning the ridge beam as a swept gold-dark cylinder along the roof top with decorative onigawara end-caps as spheres, then adding a hanging bell at the front and a wooden slatted offering box placed on the ground near the shrine steps.

Simplifying to a rope hanging from a front beam at the porch, with two red support posts flanking the entrance to hold up the roof overhang.

Now I'm laying out the remaining scene elements: stone lanterns flanking the path, a sakura tree at the back left, fox statue guardians on pedestals before the shrine, offerings like sake barrels, mochi, fruit, candles, and flower bowls placed on either side, plus an ema plaque rack positioned off to the side.

I'm also hanging chochin lanterns from the torii crossbeam, a sagging shimenawa rope strung between the pillars with dangling shide paper cards, and defining the gravel ground disc with a mossy rounded rim using a lathe profile roughly twice the width of the torii itself.

Reducing the base radius to 3.2, I'm standardizing a ground height constant so all props sit consistently at that level, with tree placement and sinking offsets adjusted accordingly. I'm also sketching generic helper functions for boxes, cylinders, and spheres that take center coordinates and dimensions, plus reasoning through how bone/joint auto-assignment will grab the nearest parts.

To avoid misbinding hinge joints to unintended nearby pillars or parts, I'm deciding to make every helper explicitly default to bone: root unless overridden, applying this to sweeps, cards, lathes, and extrudes alike. I'm also working out the hinge joint setup for the lantern swing, placing the chochin joint and parenting its parts to root.

Now I'm sketching out the SVG textures: a dark plaque with a gold swirl emblem, a cream lattice door panel with red kumiko diamonds, and a wooden ema plaque with a painted fox face, planning to use double-sided planes for the ema so it reads correctly when hung.

Writing more shide and lantern decals...

Petals get frames with random directions and leaning cards, plus fallen petals mirrored flat on the ground; trunk gets a bark-grain cel paint. For the kitsune fox statues, I'm assembling stone bodies from scaled spheres, cone ears and snout, a swept tail, and a gold collar, mirrored on both sides and facing toward the torii path at x=±0.95.

Working out the fox placement and facing direction relative to the torii and shrine, then building a stone lantern function with hexagonal base, shaft, collar ring, and firebox with glowing window insets on each face.

Working out the hex roof profile and the hoju finial with a stone sphere and cone, then stacking up the lantern's heights section by section — base, shaft, collar, platform, firebox, roof, hoju — scaled to around 1.5m like a real toro lantern. For the chochin lantern I'm shaping a scaled glowing sphere with gold-black cylinder caps top and bottom.

Now I'm positioning two hanging chochin lanterns at x=-0.5 and x=0.5 off the torii's nuki beam, working out the string length and joint placement so they hang at the right height without clipping the beam, and figuring out where the shimenawa sacred rope and plaque should sit relative to the nuki so nothing overlaps.

Instead of a sagging rope across the nuki, I'm wrapping each pillar with a closed rope ring with hanging shide paper strips, then starting to model a lathed sake barrel offering with bulging profile and gold bands.

Adding more offerings...

Now I'm laying out the wooden offering table with box legs, an ema rack with posts, crossbar, and hanging plaque boxes positioned off to the side, and considering a subtle teal glowing spiral sweep for a wind effect near the gold orbs.

I'm also planning the stepping-stone path with jittered box sizes and mottled stone coloring running down the scene, plus scattering small rocks and grass tuft cards along the edges for texture.

Now I'm adding scattered bamboo-grass frames avoiding the central path, moss patches, shrine entrance steps, and considering details like sweep ropes and lathe geometry parameters for the shrine structure.

Checking which imports are actually used to avoid unused-variable errors, then defining typed helper functions with position, rotation, scale, and bone parameters for placing geometry.

Writing full part-building code...

Defining color palette...

Still building torii structure...

I'm deciding to color the kasagi black (lacquer) with gold tip caps, while the shimaki stays vermilion below it, making sure the pillars still clear the shimaki's bottom edge at their current height.

Still placing gold tip boxes and plaque dimensions...

Adding the chochin lanterns now, with hinge joints, hanging string rods, top caps, and the lantern body as a scaled sphere with its own texture and rotation.

Now I'm adding the tassel sweep, bottom cap, and segment counts for the sphere, then moving to the shimenawa rope rings around the pillars with wobbled catmull curves and twisted rope bands.

For the shide paper cards, I'm placing frames at four points around the ring and calling one function to attach all cards with a leaning flow orientation. Then I'm scattering path stones along the approach with randomized size and rotation jitter using a seeded RNG.

I'm now checking for overlaps between the path stones, shrine steps, and saisen box -- adjusting z-positions so the step box, offering box, and final path stone don't intersect near the shrine front.

Simplifying to just one step plus the base: a single step box positioned around z=-0.78 with height 0.1, sitting between the end of the stone path at -0.61 and the base front, while I check it doesn't overlap the base region starting at -1.15.

Now I'm working out whether to add a saisen offering box or table near the porch, and adjusting the porch post positions and base depth so the posts land on the base top without colliding with the step — widening the base depth to roughly 1.5 centered near z=-1.8 so everything fits.

Now I'm checking the roof clearance over the porch posts—with body base at G+0.3 and height 0.9, the ridge sits at y=1.85, and tracing the slab slope down to x=0.55 gives an underside around 1.5, so I need the posts (height 1.15, topping at G+1.45) to clear that properly.

Working through the kamoi box placement near y=1.42, the bell's hanging joint, and the roof slab's rotation geometry to confirm the eaves extend above and beyond the body walls. Then I'm sketching the gable triangle profile at the front, checking its slope against the roof underside at several x-values to make sure the triangle fits flush beneath the overhang.

I'm adjusting the apex height to 0.48 so it sits just under the roof surface without poking through, then adding a ridge cylinder sweeping along the roof's length with gold finial spheres at the ends, plus an upward gold spike for the onigawara ornament. I'm also planning gold bargeboard trims running along the eaves at each end of the roof slab.

Now I'm working out the world-space position for these end trims by computing where the slab's local edge maps through its rotation, then mirroring for the opposite side. For the front I'm adding two door planes positioned symmetrically at the front face, sized and textured white, while the back gets a solid wood body box with corner posts.

I'm placing vertical corner posts and a horizontal rail box at the top, giving the main body cream-colored walls, and adding a gold lattice frame plus knob spheres to the doors. Then I'm adding a porch floor and an offering box near the front with a dark slotted top and gold coin details.

Now I'm shaping the bell: a hinge joint and rope with alternating red-and-white color bands connecting to a lathed bell profile positioned above the porch, defining the curved cross-section that forms its bulbous shape.

Placing torii pillars at x±1.0, z=1, keeping distance from the path reasonable. Then positioning the fox statues near x±0.85-0.95 at z around -0.1, standing beside the path, with stone lanterns slightly further out at x±1.7, z=0.2.

Building the fox statue function with pedestal, sitting body, haunches, front legs, and head geometry...

Still placing props and features...

Adding offering table details: a cream plate with mochi stack, oranges with green leaves, a blue-white lathed vase with pink and yellow blossoms, a tea cup, and two candles with glowing flame cones on gold holders.

On the right side I'm placing straw bales and sake barrels with gold hoops and red labels, plus a small gold incense burner on three legs with glowing ember-tipped sticks, positioning everything near the torii pillars without blocking the path.

Now I'm designing an ema rack with two posts and a crossbar, topped with a small tilted roof slab, and hanging five small wooden ema plaques from short rods across the top beam, with a second lower crossbar for additional plaques.

For the sakura tree, I'm building a curved trunk sweep tapering from thick at the base to thin at top, then adding a couple of branch sweeps extending outward and upward -- though I need to check whether the rightward branch would clash with the shrine roof above.

Still writing canopy blobs...

I'm checking that fallen petals stay within the scene bounds relative to the tree position, finding I need to expand the base lathe radius to 3.7 and shrink petal scatter radius so everything stays inside 3.6. Now I'm sketching a grass tuft texture using an SVG viewBox.

Writing scatter logic for grass positions...

Then I'll add floating glowing teal orbs near the shrine as small spheres for atmosphere.

I'm also sweeping a small spiral swirl shape near the shrine using a spiral path with increasing radius and pitch, checking it won't collide with the stone path or fox position since its radius stays small.

Now I'm adding gold filigree details to the lantern roof and shrine door, then writing the SVG texture string for the plaque, including its border, circle emblem, and a decorative gold swirl motif inside.

Next I'm sketching out the door texture at a larger size, planning a warm cream background with a gold frame and a red kumiko lattice pattern spaced evenly across it.

For the ema plaque, I'm designing a pentagon-shaped wooden shape with a warm brown fill and darker outline, then adding a stylized fox face inside with triangular ears and curved features in red and white.

Now I'm sketching a shide (sacred paper streamer) as a white zigzag ribbon shape with a subtle beige outline, simplifying the path so the folds read clearly without self-intersection issues.

Next I'm designing a petal icon as a rounded teardrop shape in pink with a darker center vein stroke, scaling the stroke width proportionally for larger sizes. For grass, I'm drawing three simple blade paths in two shades of green within a tall narrow viewbox.

For the chochin lantern, I'm using a red-orange base with darker vertical rib lines at regular intervals, gold bands at the top and bottom, and a central circular glyph with a swirl design, considering how it reads when rotated to face forward.

Now I'm building the stone lantern geometry -- stacking toroidal bases, cylindrical shafts, and collar sections with flat shading, computing each piece's vertical offset to stack correctly.

Then I'm assembling the firebox with corner posts, a glowing warm-colored core, and framing plates above and below, before lathing the pagoda-style roof profile and topping it with a gold finial sphere.

Now I'm defining a sake barrel helper using a lathe profile for the barrel shape with wood coloring and torus hoops positioned at interpolated radii along the height.

Now it's time to write everything, with around 250 parts total. I'm setting up a sweep helper function that builds tube-like shapes from path points and radius values, using the sweep API's typed radius parameter that accepts either a number or a pair.

I'm also sketching helper types for spirals, frames for placing cards, and a random direction function that normalizes points on a sphere. Then I'm finalizing the piece, returning the root node, and tidying unused variables like INK so it's used consistently for eyes and other ink-colored details.

Now I'm working through final geometry details: cylinder helper argument order, the rack and cords, and a lathed incense burner profile with legs and sticks, checking that the profile points don't self-intersect.

Adding smoke wisps and glowing ember tips...

Then I'll double-check the bone/joint typing before writing out the final file.
